study_identification.title: Evidence for embracing normative modeling

study_characteristics.study_objective: To expand the normative model repository with models of structural surface area and functional connectivity, and to compare the utility of normative modeling features against raw data features in benchmarking tasks.
study_characteristics.study_design_other: Methodological paper with cross-sectional analysis for benchmarking tasks.

dataset_name.answer: Multi-site aggregated dataset (ABCD; CAMCAN; CMI-HBN; HCP-Aging; HCP-Development; HCP-Early Psychosis; HCP-Young Adult; NKI-RS; OpenNeuro; PNC; and UKBiobank)

hc_age.answer: Age range: 2-100 years. Detailed age information per site is available in Supplementary file 1 and 2.

hc_sex.answer: Detailed sex distribution per site is available in Supplementary file 1 and 2.

quality_checking_detail.answer: High-quality was defined for structural images as the lack of any artifacts such as ghosting or ringing, that Freesurfer surface reconstruction was able to run successfully, and that the Euler number was below a chosen threshold (rescaled Euler < 10). High-quality functional data was defined as having a high-quality structural MRI and at least 5 min of low motion data (framewise displacement < 0.5 mm). Manual inspection was also performed.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: Site variation was modeled using fixed effects in the Bayesian Linear Regression model. The covariates used to train the normative models included age, sex, data quality metric (Euler number or mean framewise displacement), and site.

model_origin_detail.answer: The study uses and expands a publicly shared repository of pre-trained normative models. The structural models were estimated on approx. 58,000 subjects, and the new functional models on approx. 22,000 subjects. The models are available at https://github.com/predictive-clinical-neuroscience/braincharts.

response_variable.answer: Cortical thickness; Subcortical volume; Surface area; Functional connectivity (Yeo-17 and Smith-10 atlases)

predictor_variables.answer: Age; Sex; Data quality metric (Euler number or mean framewise displacement); Site

predictor_effects.answer: Site was modeled as a fixed effect. Age was modeled using a B-spline basis expansion to capture non-linear effects.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The paper explicitly states that nuisance variables including site, age, sex, and motion were modeled.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: The covariates used to train the structural normative models included age, sex, data quality metric (Euler number), and site.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The paper uses a 10-fold cross-validation framework for the classification task.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: The evaluation metric for the classification task is an area under the receiving operator curve (AUC) averaged across all folds within a 10-fold cross-validation framework.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The paper used a held-out test set for model evaluation.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: Evaluation of the functional normative models was performed in a test set (20% of the training set)...

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The paper used transfer sets (COBRE and UMich) which were not seen by the model during training.
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: We transferred the functional normative models to the datasets used in this work for benchmarking (Table 1) to generate deviation (Z) scores. HCP was included in the initial training (half of the sample was held out in the test set), while the UMich and COBRE datasets were not included in the training and can be considered as examples of transfer to new, unseen sites.

clinical_groups_n.answer: COBRE: 124 (schizophrenia vs control); UMich: 89 (schizophrenia vs control)

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Mass univariate group difference testing (two-sample independent t-tests), multivariate prediction - classification (Support Vector Classification), and multivariate prediction - regression (Principal Component Regression).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Normative modeling features show benefits over raw data features in group difference testing, classification, and regression tasks, with the strongest evidence in group difference testing.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: In group difference testing, normative modeling found numerous significant group differences (FDR p < 0.05) while raw data showed none. In classification, cortical thickness deviation scores achieved 87% AUC, significantly better than raw data (43% AUC). In regression, deviation scores showed a modest, non-significant improvement in predicting general cognitive ability.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The representation of functional connectivity using the Yeo-17 atlas is a simplification. The reference cohort is likely overrepresentative of European-ancestry populations. The term 'normative' is used in a statistical sense and not a moral or ethical one.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The authors have developed a user-friendly interface (https://pcnportal.dccn.nl/) for transferring the pre-trained normative models to new samples without requiring programming.

general_notes.general_notes: Pre-trained models and analysis scripts are publicly available on GitHub. The paper provides a comprehensive evaluation of the benefits of using normative modeling in neuroimaging research.
